correctness.rationale: The proof checks the vertex-to-edge gradient intertwining and the exact symmetric Markov generator for all positive vertex masses. Every zero-sum edge gradient has an exact two-state extreme decomposition; the sharp derivative and all-time semigroup criterion follow. For n≥7 the distant-edge graph is connected nonbipartite, and summing its pair constraints gives a zero weighted Laplacian, hence constant weights. For n≤6, strict near-pair contraction and a six-cycle antiperiodic construction establish the opposite regime. The uniform-mass inequalities are obtained by direct explicit substitution. Exact rational checks in verify.py support finite identities, not infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Whether discrete heat flow decreases a chosen weighted BV seminorm at all times is a natural stability and weighting-design problem. The result identifies a sharp graph-size structural obstruction: for all n≥7 and any positive vertex masses, a nonuniform positive edge weight forces initial increase of some genuine step signal, whereas each shorter cycle admits nonuniform contractive weights. The complete small-n inequalities and an exact sharp initial growth coefficient make the boundary operational and nontrivial; this is not mere renaming of the weighted Dobrushin formula.
